title: Expose capability matrix and profile endpoint for versioned models
creator: Priya Shah
description: Add a first-class, discoverable API surface that publishes model capability metadata and performance profiles tied to specific model versions. The goal is to allow clients and routing logic to programmatically enumerate what a model variant supports (features, limits, recommended quantization), its context window and tokenization constraints, and standardized perf profiles (p50/p95 latencies, tokens/sec, memory footprint) for representative sequence lengths. This is intended to unblock version pinning in routing policies, automated fallbacks, and provide data for Redwood Optimize recommendations.
motivation: Currently we surface model names and a free-text manifest during onboarding, but downstream systems (routing, console, optimize) lack structured, versioned metadata to make deterministic decisions. Exposing machine-readable capability+profile contracts will reduce runtime surprises, enable safe automatic fallback, and give customers more transparent SLAs per version.
api_schema_changes: Introduce GET /v1/models -> returns list of model names with available versions and metadata refs
Introduce GET /v1/models/{model}/versions/{version}/profile -> returns structured capability matrix and perf profile for that exact version

Profile schema includes: capabilities (chat, streaming, function-calling, embeddings), limits (tokens, requests/sec), context_window, tokenization_hint, memory_peaks_by_seqlen (map seq_len->MB), perf_by_seqlen (map seq_len->{p50_ms,p95_ms,tokens_per_sec}), quantization_recommendation (e.g., int8, int4), compatibility_tags (fallback-to: variant-a, variant-b), and deprecation timestamp
Add model.manifest.versioned_url field pointing to the canonical profile endpoint for UI and SDKs
Backward-compatibility: server MUST still accept requests with previous manifest shapes; clients opt-in to versioned profiles by requesting the new endpoints
acceptance_criteria: Schema documented in the API spec (OpenAPI) and reviewed by SDK owners
Impl: new endpoints implemented behind feature flag with mocked data for 2 curated open models
Routing layer can call the profile endpoint and make a deterministic decision to pin to a compatible variant
Console shows per-version profile on the model details page and signals when a pinned version is deprecated
Performance profiles include p50/p95 for at least three sequence lengths (64, 512, 2048) and memory estimates
Migration plan written: how older manifests are indexed and how to handle missing profile data
implementation_notes: Server: Add profiles service that stores canonical profiles in DynamoDB with versioned keys. Populate initial profiles from onboarding pipeline and model bench runs. Expose via new controllers under /v1/models. Update model registry to store profile_url. Routing: add a ProfileCache in the router with TTL and stale-while-revalidate behavior. Console: fetch & render profile; show deprecation banner if deprecation timestamp < 90 days. SDKs: add helper to fetch and normalize profiles into client-side routing decisions.
data_migration_plan: Backfill pipeline will run: 1) identify models missing profiles; 2) spawn bench jobs to generate perf_by_seqlen for 3 target seq lens; 3) synthesize capability flags from onboarding metadata; 4) write profiles to store. Backfill will be rate-limited to avoid saturating bench infra.
security_considerations: Profiles may reveal performance characteristics that could be abused to fingerprint hardware or model internals. Restrict detailed perf_by_seqlen to authenticated tenants and redact precise p95 for public listings. Audit logging required for profile updates. KMS keys for profile writes enforced for private deployments.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged launch for internal tenants; 2) Invite select external beta customers and SDK partners; 3) Gate full rollout on successful backfill and no critical issues for 2 weeks. Deprecation policy: publishers can set a deprecation timestamp; router treats deprecated versions as lower priority for automatic pinning after date passes.
open_questions: Do we need multi-region replication of profiles for low-latency routing?
What exact granularity of seq_len buckets do we publish (64/128/512/1024/2048 vs. a continuous curve)?
Should quantization_recommendation be prescriptive (exact flags) or advisory commentary?
How do we signal partial profiles when bench data isn't yet available for a new version?
dependencies_notes: Depends on kernel selection telemetry from ENG-32456 for accurate memory_peak estimates. Also depends on model manifest versioning work in ENG-28321 to ensure stable version identifiers.
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema validation, integration tests for profile endpoints with mocked bench outputs, e2e test that router pins to fallback variant when a profile indicates incompatibility, load tests to ensure profile cache scales to routing QPS.
